newsitem.title: MEXICO: Quake measuring 5.9 rocks southern Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Quake measuring 5.9 rocks southern Mexico.

text.p: A large earthquake, measuring up to 5.9 on the open-ended Richter scale, rocked southern Mexico early on Tuesday but there were no immediate reports of deaths or damage, authorities and reports said.
"The automatic reading we have is in the range of 5.8 to 5.9 near the coast of Chiapas," said Jim Taggart, of the U.S. National Earthquake Information Service in Golden, Colorado.
"We have not got a precise reading yet, we are still working out the details, but it was pretty powerful," Taggart told Reuters in a telephone interview.
News reports in Mexico said the quake was felt around 0642 local (0742 EST/1242 GMT) throughout the southern part of the country and even in parts of the capital.

National radio network Radio Red said their correspondents reported the quake frightened local populations in the states of Tabasco, Oaxaca and Chiapas, including the colonial tourist city of San Cristobal de las Casas.
But there were no immediate reports of deaths or damage from the regions, which are some 480 miles (800 km) southeast of Mexico City.
